Testing is only authorized on the targets listed as in scope. Any domain/property of Aiven not listed in the targets section is out of scope. This includes any/all subdomains not listed above.

Aiven's Permission Model

  • Permissions that are granted in the API are intentionally granted, whether or not they are "greyed out" or accessible in the console.

Program Rules

  • Only use your @bugcrowdninja email addresses for registering testing accounts.
  • Social engineering (e.g. phishing, vishing, smishing) is prohibited.
  • You are testing on production. For example, do not target other users' data (instead, please use one of your other sets of credentials), delete/remove/edit parts of the site, engage any sort of DoS or DDoS attack, and/or compromise any target's ability to function for other users.

Exploit Chain Testing

  • Cross-account access . We are interested in avenues to make authenticated access to other accounts' services where the other account has not allowed this access - please use only other accounts that you own, not random customers.

Out of Scope

  • Only services you create by yourself - for example, PostgreSQL, Kafka and Grafana - are in-scope. Other services in aivencloud.com domain not created by you are explicitly out of scope, as those are our customers' services.
  • Functionality provided through third parties is out of scope. This includes Calendly, Qualified, Salesforce, and similar.
  • Rate limiting issues
  • Unreported or very recently reported issues (0day), or issues for which no patch is available, against software not published by Aiven.

Safe Harbor

When conducting vulnerability research according to this policy, we consider this research to be:

  • Authorized in accordance with the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA).
  • Lawful, helpful to the overall security of the Internet, and conducted in good faith.
